spec.rawSql:
WITH pano AS (
  SELECT * FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/amsterdam-panoramas/panoramas.parquet')
), pick AS (
  -- The panorama picked on the map (of any year), or the middle of Dam.
  SELECT longitude, latitude FROM (
    SELECT longitude, latitude, 0 AS rank FROM pano WHERE pano_id = $pano
    UNION ALL SELECT 4.893095, 52.372970, 1
  ) ORDER BY rank LIMIT 1
), shown AS (
  -- Of the year picked, the panorama nearest it: a change of year stays on the spot.
  SELECT pano.* FROM pano, pick
  WHERE pano.year = CAST($year AS INTEGER)
  ORDER BY ((pano.longitude - pick.longitude) * 0.61) ^ 2 + (pano.latitude - pick.latitude) ^ 2
  LIMIT 1
), cam AS (
  -- Metres round the camera (x east, y north), 2.5 m over the ground the LiDAR gives under it.
  SELECT longitude AS lon0, latitude AS lat0, cos(radians(latitude)) * 111320 AS kx,
         110574.0 AS ky, ground_nap + 2.5 AS z0
  FROM shown
), footprints AS (
  SELECT b.*, ST_TransScale(ST_GeomFromText(b.geometry), -cam.lon0, -cam.lat0, cam.kx, cam.ky) AS g
  FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/amsterdam-panoramas/buildings.parquet') b, cam
), facades AS (
  -- Buildings within 60 m, monuments within 150 m: the point of the façade nearest the camera.
  SELECT *, ST_ClosestPoint(g, ST_Point(0, 0)) AS q
  FROM footprints
  WHERE (ST_DWithin(g, ST_Point(0, 0), 60) OR (monument IS NOT NULL AND ST_DWithin(g, ST_Point(0, 0), 150)))
    AND NOT ST_Contains(g, ST_Point(0, 0))
), candidates AS (
  -- A façade aimed at half its height (at most 10 m up), a tree at 60 % of its height, a
  -- monument at 70 %.
  SELECT 'building' AS kind, building_id AS id, building_id AS own, ST_X(q) AS x, ST_Y(q) AS y,
         ground_nap + least(coalesce(height_lidar, 12) * 0.5, 10) AS z,
         coalesce(split_part(monument, ',', 1), built::VARCHAR) AS label,
         concat_ws(' · ', monument, monument_status, 'built ' || built, 'architect ' || architect,
                   'LiDAR height ' || round(height_lidar)::INTEGER || ' m') AS detail
  FROM facades
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'tree', tree_id, NULL, (longitude - lon0) * kx, (latitude - lat0) * ky,
         ground_nap + 0.6 * coalesce(height_lidar, class_m, 8),
         coalesce(split_part(species, ' ', 1), 'Tree'),
         concat_ws(' · ', coalesce(species, 'a tree'), 'planted ' || planted,
                   'LiDAR height ' || round(height_lidar)::INTEGER || ' m')
  FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/amsterdam-panoramas/trees.parquet'), cam
  WHERE ((longitude - lon0) * kx) ^ 2 + ((latitude - lat0) * ky) ^ 2 BETWEEN 1 AND 45 ^ 2
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'monument', monument_id, NULL, (longitude - lon0) * kx, (latitude - lat0) * ky,
         ground_nap + greatest(0.7 * height_lidar, 1.5),
         name,
         concat_ws(' · ', name, status, 'architect ' || architect,
                   'LiDAR height ' || round(height_lidar)::INTEGER || ' m')
  FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/amsterdam-panoramas/monuments.parquet'), cam
  WHERE ((longitude - lon0) * kx) ^ 2 + ((latitude - lat0) * ky) ^ 2 BETWEEN 1 AND 150 ^ 2
), measured AS (
  SELECT c.*, sqrt(x * x + y * y) AS distance_m FROM candidates c
), seen AS (
  -- In sight: the line from the camera to it (stopped 0.5 m short) crosses no other footprint.
  SELECT m.* FROM measured m
  WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM footprints f
    WHERE f.building_id IS DISTINCT FROM m.own
      AND ST_Intersects(f.g, ST_MakeLine(ST_Point(0, 0),
            ST_Point(m.x * (1 - 0.5 / m.distance_m), m.y * (1 - 0.5 / m.distance_m))))
  )
)
SELECT count(*) AS "In sight" FROM seen

options.content:
**What it is.** Dam Square in Amsterdam and the streets round it, 450 m a side, as a city keeps it: the 360° panoramas its car takes of every street each year, the national LiDAR survey, and its registers of buildings, monuments and trees, each placed in the others. Click a panorama on the map to see it beside it; the viewer marks on the picture what the registers know of what it shows, and the map shows where it looks.

**The panoramas.** Gemeente Amsterdam, *Panoramabeelden* ([api.data.amsterdam.nl/panorama](https://api.data.amsterdam.nl/panorama/panoramas/), CC BY 4.0): 11,597 in the box, from June 2016 to July 2025, one every 5 m along each street (the 2017 and 2021 missions also from the water), faces and number plates blurred by the city. Each picture is equirectangular with north in the middle and the horizon level, so a thing's place in it is its bearing and the angle up to it. The browser reads the 4,000 px picture from the city; nothing of it is stored here. The 2022 mission ran into April 2023, and there is no 2023 mission: the year is the city's.

**The LiDAR.** AHN5, *Actueel Hoogtebestand Nederland* (CC0), flown in 2023: 4.5 million points in the box (about 22 a square metre), read from its 1 km cloud-optimised tile by ranges and written as 3D Tiles (`datasets/amsterdam-panoramas/build.sh`), the street level (+1.29 m NAP) at the map's ground. Coloured from the aerial photograph *Luchtfoto Actueel Ortho* of Beeldmateriaal Nederland / Kadaster (PDOK, [opendata.beeldmateriaal.nl](https://opendata.beeldmateriaal.nl), CC BY 4.0), as AHN's coloured clouds are: a wall takes the colour of the roof or street beside it seen from above. The LiDAR also gives every height here: a tree's is the highest vegetation return within 3 m of its trunk over the ground there, a building's the 90th percentile of its roof over the ground beside it, the ground under each panorama the mean of the ground returns within 1.5 m.

**The registers.** Gemeente Amsterdam at [api.data.amsterdam.nl](https://api.data.amsterdam.nl/v1/), published as public data with no licence named beyond that: BAG buildings (year built, footprint), the monument register (name, Rijksmonument or Gemeentelijk monument, architect; a building takes the monument on most of its footprint), the tree register (species, year planted, height class). Read once by the dataset's build, in November 2026.

**What is in sight.** From the camera, 2.5 m over the ground: buildings within 60 m (monuments within 150 m) at the point of their façade nearest it, trees within 45 m, monuments that are not a building within 150 m, kept when the straight line to them crosses no other building's footprint. Footprints only: a low wall or a tram shelter hides nothing, and a tree behind another tree is still marked.

**Built** with the dataset's build on the instance; the panoramas grow by a mission a year: run the build again to follow them.

spec.rawSql:
-- Every panorama of the year picked, at the camera's height (2.5 m): click one to see it in
-- 360° beside the map.
SELECT p.pano_id, p.longitude, p.latitude, p.ground_nap - m.street_nap + 2.5 AS altitude,
       'taken ' || strftime(timezone('Europe/Amsterdam', p.taken), '%-d %b %Y') AS taken_on
FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/amsterdam-panoramas/panoramas.parquet') p, read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/amsterdam-panoramas/meta.parquet') m
WHERE p.year = CAST($year AS INTEGER)

WITH pano AS (
  SELECT * FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/amsterdam-panoramas/panoramas.parquet')
), pick AS (
  -- The panorama picked on the map (of any year), or the middle of Dam.
  SELECT longitude, latitude FROM (
    SELECT longitude, latitude, 0 AS rank FROM pano WHERE pano_id = $pano
    UNION ALL SELECT 4.893095, 52.372970, 1
  ) ORDER BY rank LIMIT 1
), shown AS (
  -- Of the year picked, the panorama nearest it: a change of year stays on the spot.
  SELECT pano.* FROM pano, pick
  WHERE pano.year = CAST($year AS INTEGER)
  ORDER BY ((pano.longitude - pick.longitude) * 0.61) ^ 2 + (pano.latitude - pick.latitude) ^ 2
  LIMIT 1
), cone AS (
  SELECT s.longitude AS lon0, s.latitude AS lat0, cos(radians(s.latitude)) * 111320 AS kx,
         round(s.ground_nap - m.street_nap + 2.5, 2) AS z,
         coalesce(try_cast(nullif($look, '') AS DOUBLE), 0) AS look,
         least(greatest(coalesce(try_cast(nullif($fov, '') AS DOUBLE), 100), 20), 140) AS fov
  FROM shown s, read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/amsterdam-panoramas/meta.parquet') m
)
-- Where the viewer looks from the panorama shown: a 30 m wedge as wide as its view and turned
-- as it is ($look and $fov, which the viewer writes when it stops), at the camera's height
-- (the square's ground rises, and its points would cover a wedge laid on it).
SELECT '{"type":"Polygon","coordinates":[[[' || lon0 || ',' || lat0 || ',' || z || '],' ||
       array_to_string(list_transform(range(0, 25), lambda i:
         '[' || (lon0 + 30 * sin(radians(look - fov / 2 + fov * i / 24)) / kx) || ',' ||
         (lat0 + 30 * cos(radians(look - fov / 2 + fov * i / 24)) / 110574) || ',' || z || ']'), ',') ||
       ',[' || lon0 || ',' || lat0 || ',' || z || ']]]}' AS geometry,
       'looking ' || round(look)::INTEGER || '°' AS view
FROM cone

-- The city's trees, on top of their crowns (the height the LiDAR measures over the ground
-- round the trunk, from the street level the point cloud stands on).
SELECT t.longitude, t.latitude, coalesce(t.species, 'unknown') AS species, t.planted,
       t.height_lidar AS height_m,
       t.ground_nap - m.street_nap + coalesce(t.height_lidar, t.class_m, 8) AS altitude
FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/amsterdam-panoramas/trees.parquet') t, read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/amsterdam-panoramas/meta.parquet') m

spec.description: The national LiDAR survey (AHN5) of the 450 m round Dam Square as a point cloud, coloured from the aerial photograph, with the city's trees on their crowns (green) and every panorama of the year picked (blue, at the camera's height). Click one to see it beside the map; the orange wedge is where the viewer looks.
spec.title: Dam Square in LiDAR: click a panorama

WITH pano AS (

-- The panorama shown, and the panorama picked it was found for (the viewer waits for rows that

       strftime(timezone('Europe/Amsterdam', s.taken), '%-d %B %Y, %H:%M') AS taken_on,
       round(sqrt(((s.longitude - p.longitude) * 0.61 * 111320) ^ 2 + ((s.latitude - p.latitude) * 110574) ^ 2), 1) AS from_pick_m

  ORDER BY ((pano.longitude - pick.longitude) * 0.61) ^ 2 + (pano.latitude - pick.latitude) ^ 2

  -- Metres round the camera (x east, y north), 2.5 m over the ground the LiDAR gives under it.
  SELECT longitude AS lon0, latitude AS lat0, cos(radians(latitude)) * 111320 AS kx,

SELECT kind, id, label, detail, round(distance_m, 1) AS distance_m,
       round(degrees(atan2(x, y)), 2) AS yaw, round(degrees(atan2(z - z0, distance_m)), 2) AS pitch
FROM seen, cam
ORDER BY distance_m DESC

WITH pano AS (
  SELECT * FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/amsterdam-panoramas/panoramas.parquet')
), pick AS (
  -- The panorama picked on the map (of any year), or the middle of Dam.
  SELECT longitude, latitude FROM (
    SELECT longitude, latitude, 0 AS rank FROM pano WHERE pano_id = $pano
    UNION ALL SELECT 4.893095, 52.372970, 1
  ) ORDER BY rank LIMIT 1
), shown AS (
  -- Of the year picked, the panorama nearest it: a change of year stays on the spot.
  SELECT pano.* FROM pano, pick
  WHERE pano.year = CAST($year AS INTEGER)
  ORDER BY ((pano.longitude - pick.longitude) * 0.61) ^ 2 + (pano.latitude - pick.latitude) ^ 2
  LIMIT 1
), near AS (
  SELECT p.pano_id, (p.longitude - s.longitude) * cos(radians(s.latitude)) * 111320 AS x,
         (p.latitude - s.latitude) * 110574 AS y
  FROM pano p, shown s
  WHERE p.year = s.year AND p.pano_id <> s.pano_id
    AND abs(p.latitude - s.latitude) < 0.0003 AND abs(p.longitude - s.longitude) < 0.0005
), measured AS (
  SELECT *, sqrt(x * x + y * y) AS distance_m, degrees(atan2(x, y)) AS yaw FROM near
)
-- The steps on: the nearest panorama of the same year 2 to 25 m away in each eighth of the
-- compass.
SELECT pano_id, round(yaw, 1) AS yaw, round(distance_m, 1) AS distance_m
FROM measured
WHERE distance_m BETWEEN 2 AND 25
QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY floor(((yaw + 382.5) % 360) / 45) ORDER BY distance_m) = 1

WITH pano AS (
  SELECT * FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/amsterdam-panoramas/panoramas.parquet')
), pick AS (
  -- The panorama picked on the map (of any year), or the middle of Dam.
  SELECT longitude, latitude FROM (
    SELECT longitude, latitude, 0 AS rank FROM pano WHERE pano_id = $pano
    UNION ALL SELECT 4.893095, 52.372970, 1
  ) ORDER BY rank LIMIT 1
), shown AS (
  -- Of the year picked, the panorama nearest it: a change of year stays on the spot.
  SELECT pano.* FROM pano, pick
  WHERE pano.year = CAST($year AS INTEGER)
  ORDER BY ((pano.longitude - pick.longitude) * 0.61) ^ 2 + (pano.latitude - pick.latitude) ^ 2
  LIMIT 1
)
-- The same spot in other years: each year's panorama nearest the one shown, within 25 m.
SELECT p.year, p.pano_id,
       strftime(timezone('Europe/Amsterdam', p.taken), '%b %Y') AS taken_on,
       round(sqrt(((p.longitude - s.longitude) * 0.61 * 111320) ^ 2 + ((p.latitude - s.latitude) * 110574) ^ 2), 1) AS distance_m
FROM pano p, shown s
WHERE abs(p.latitude - s.latitude) < 0.00025 AND abs(p.longitude - s.longitude) < 0.0004
QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY p.year ORDER BY distance_m) = 1 AND distance_m <= 25
ORDER BY p.year

spec.description: The city's 360° panorama nearest the one picked, of the year picked, read by the browser from the city (4,000 px, faces and plates blurred): drag to look round, scroll to zoom. On it, what is in sight from the camera, placed by bearing and height: monuments and buildings with the year they were built, trees with their species, each with the height the LiDAR measures (hover for the rest). The white circles on the street step to the next panorama; the years under it show the same spot in another year.
spec.title: The panorama in 360°, with what the city knows of what it shows
Dam Square in 360°: panoramas, LiDAR and the city's registers

spec.definition:
